findings.specText: story-026 (2dc2426): "The old transfer is removed, not kept as a fallback." / NatSpec :58-59: "That leg has been REMOVED, not kept as a fallback." / NatSpec :68-69: "Once a nudge share is actually payable there are three failure modes, all deliberate and loud (there is no try/catch envelope here)"
findings.actualBehavior: The implementation is exactly faithful: with nudgeSplit > 0, claim() unconditionally calls out to nudgeStreamer, and reverts NudgeStreamerNotConfigured when it is unset or bubbles NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered() when the (nudge, rewardToken) stream is not registered.
findings.deviation: No deviation — the STORY'S OWN INTENT is the exposure. Story-026 deliberately makes an external, owner-configured, post-deploy-defaulted-to-zero contract a hard precondition of claim(), which is SYA's only permissionless entry point and the only path by which yield-strategy surplus is skimmed and phlimbo is funded. A pre-story SYA whose owner sets nudgeSplit > 0 before setNudgeStreamer has a fully bricked claim rail; the whole conversion pipeline (and every downstream ClaimArbitrage run) stalls until the owner acts. Law 1 overrides Law 2: a faithful implementation of a no-fallback mandatory-dependency design is still flagged as the unsafe story, not blessed. Mitigating: the failure is loud, non-value-destroying, and owner-recoverable via setNudgeSplit(0) / setNudgeStreamer + registerStream — which is why this is potential-medium (availability), not High.

findings.specText: NatSpec :68-79: "Once a nudge share is actually payable there are three failure modes ... 3. Repointing the sink via `setNudgeAddress` re-arms exactly that failure mode: register the new `(sink, rewardToken)` pair on the streamer FIRST." and "### Required ops ordering ... 1. `nudge.setNudgeTokenWhitelist(rewardToken, true)` ... 2. `nudgeStreamer.registerStream(nudge, rewardToken, duration)` ... 3. `this.setNudgeAddress(nudge)` and `this.setNudgeStreamer(nudgeStreamer)` ... 4. `nudge.setNudgeStreamer(nudgeStreamer)`"
findings.actualBehavior: NudgeStreamer keys its buffer on the PAIR (batchMinter, token) — `streams[nudge][rewardToken]`. `setRewardToken` (:417-420) rewrites the second key with no guard, no event, and no mention anywhere in the story or the NatSpec. After an owner calls setRewardToken, `streams[nudge][newRewardToken].duration == 0`, so every subsequent claim with a payable nudge share reverts NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered() — the identical brick the doc attributes solely to setNudgeAddress.
findings.deviation: The NatSpec presents a closed enumeration ("there are three failure modes") and an ordered ops runbook that together read as exhaustive, but they omit setRewardToken — a second, equally load-bearing re-arm trigger. This is a documentation-vs-code deviation in its own right: a competent, non-malicious owner following the documented runbook to the letter would still brick claim() by rotating the reward token (Law-3 footgun — the doc's own completeness claim is what makes the consequence non-obvious). Fix is documentary + ops: add setRewardToken to the trigger list, or gate it on a registered (nudge, _rewardToken) stream when nudgeSplit > 0.

findings.specText: NatSpec :73-75: "If the streamer is set but ops forgot `registerStream(nudge, rewardToken, duration)` on it, every `claim` reverts `NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered()`. **That is the accepted consequence of the mandatory-streamer decision, not an audit finding.**"
findings.actualBehavior: No story artefact records any such acceptance decision. The five [story-026] commit bodies were read in full: 3e1259b (submodule wiring), e7f8a45 (RED tests), 2dc2426 (GREEN), b14522d (gas snapshot), f704130 (submodule branch fix). 2dc2426 states the design facts ("removed, not kept as a fallback"; "scoped to the live-donation branch") but nowhere records an owner decision to ACCEPT the resulting availability exposure, and nowhere pre-adjudicates it as a non-finding. The project CLAUDE.md is silent on the nudge rail entirely. registered-projects.json carries no matching designDecision.
findings.deviation: The clause is an unsupported in-source claim (b), not traceable to a story decision (a). It is the only place in the repo where the exposure is dispositioned, and it disposes of it by asserting it is out of audit scope. Under Law 1 a source comment cannot suppress a finding — 'recall beats report-tidiness', and this comment is precisely a suppression written into the artefact under audit. Flagged so the assertion is adjudicated by the owner in the ledger rather than by the code it describes. Note the same NatSpec block simultaneously fails its own completeness bar (F-02), which weakens it as a self-certification. Remedy: either record the acceptance as a real triage decision (ledger / registered-projects designDecisions) and drop the self-exculpating sentence, or drop the claim.

findings.specText: NudgeStreamer.sol:20-24: "Buffers bursty donations per `(batchMinter, token)` and streams them linearly to zero over a configured `duration`, so that whoever calls `batchMint` right after a burst can no longer capture a disproportionate share of the reward pot."
findings.actualBehavior: The streamer throttles the RATE at which donated value arrives in the pot; it does not bound any single batcher's SHARE of what has arrived. `pullPendingStream` settles the full accrued amount to whichever batchMinter calls it, and `batchMint` then consumes the pot it finds. Below a demand threshold — i.e. whenever batchMint calls are sparse relative to `duration` — a single batcher still captures 100% of everything accrued since the last flush. 'No longer disproportionate' is therefore delivered only in the high-frequency limit; the property asserted unconditionally is not the property the code enforces.
findings.deviation: Asserted-property-vs-delivered-behaviour mismatch in the dependency whose adoption IS story-026. Scoping note (honest, and load-bearing for triage): (i) SYA's own story-026 text makes only the weaker, TRUE claim — "the batch-minter receives a smooth linear stream instead of a lumpy push" — which the code does deliver, so SYA's first-party story is faithful; (ii) the over-claim lives in lib/phoenix-nft-staking, a nested dependency whose root cause is out of scope for this project and which is separately audited (its own run-24 already characterises the streamer as a timing-throttle, not a value-cap). Reported here rather than dropped because story-026's justification for the whole migration rests on the imported claim. Recommend: filed as a documentation finding against the dependency, or suppressed as a known dependency-side characterisation — not as an SYA behaviour bug.

clearedChecks.check: INFTMinter -> INFTMinterV2 swap in untagged commit 3c9c54e ("fixed broken build") — silent semantic change?
clearedChecks.evidence: yield-claim-nft pin moved bc99ee3 -> f46a5cb in commit 39ee41e. `git ls-tree f46a5cb src/interfaces/` shows INFTMinterV2.sol and NO INFTMinter.sol — V1 was genuinely deleted upstream, so the build break is real and the swap is forced, not elective. SYA calls exactly two members of that interface: `burn(address,uint256,uint256)` (:619) and `nextIndex()` (:788). Both are declared with byte-identical signatures in old INFTMinter.sol (lines 15 and 53 of the bc99ee3 blob) and in INFTMinterV2.sol, so both selectors are unchanged and no call-site behaviour moved. INFTMinterV2's additions (mintFor, setAuthorizedMinter, replaceDispatcher) and its one removal (getDispatchers) are untouched by SYA. No semantic change was smuggled in.
clearedChecks.residualNote: One cosmetic side effect worth an ops note, not a finding: the same commit tightened the setNFTMinter NatSpec from "must ... implement INFTMinter" to "must ... implement INFTMinterV2", i.e. it narrowed a DOCUMENTED integration requirement inside an untagged 'fixed broken build' commit. The code still only requires the two unchanged selectors, so a V1-shaped minter would function while now reading as non-conformant to the doc. Harmless today; mentioned only because doc-requirement changes should not ride along in untagged build fixes.

notes: The project CLAUDE.md documents the accumulator's purpose and the ClaimArbitrage accounting but says NOTHING about the nudge split or the streamer rail. Intent for story-026 was resolvable only from commit bodies + in-source NatSpec. That is a spec-location gap, not itself a finding, but it is why F-03 matters: the in-source NatSpec is currently the sole authority on this feature and it both over-claims completeness (F-02) and self-certifies against audit (F-03).
No conflict was found between the commit bodies and the in-source NatSpec on any behavioural point; the only divergence is the NatSpec asserting a decision the commits never record (F-03).
